Introducing the Dataset

Basic Summary Statistics

bike_data%>%
  summarise( 
          min_rent = min(Rented.Bike.Count),
          avg_rent = mean(Rented.Bike.Count, na.rm= TRUE),
          med_rent = median(Rented.Bike.Count),
          max_rent = max(Rented.Bike.Count),
          sd_rent = sd(Rented.Bike.Count),
          iqr_rent = IQR(Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.25, Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.5, Rented.Bike.Count),

Exploring Temporal Variables

FUNCTIONING DAYS

bike_data %>%
  count(Functioning.Day)
##   Functioning.Day    n
## 1              No  295
## 2             Yes 8465
bike_data %>%
  group_by(Functioning.Day)%>%
  summarise(mean_func = mean(Rented.Bike.Count, na.rm = TRUE))
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   Functioning.Day mean_func
##   <chr>               <dbl>
## 1 No                     0 
## 2 Yes                  729.
bike_data %>%
  drop_na(Rented.Bike.Count, Functioning.Day) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Functioning.Day, fill = Functioning.Day)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "salmon",
                               "Yes" = "skyblue")) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Functioning Day",
       y = "Bike Renting Day",
       title = "Relationship between Rental and Functioning Day") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

From the data it can be determined that there were 295 instances of non functioning hours of the Seoul Bike Rental Service between 2017 and 2018, suggesting 12.3 days of the year the bikes were out of commission. This is approximately 3.36% of the year where bikes were unavailable to be rented.

This causes a significant drop in mean bike rentals inclusive and exclusive of the non-functioning days, where bike rental is 0. On functioning days only, the mean is 729.157 rentals per hour, however throughout the whole year the rental rate is 704.602 rentals per hour.

Exploring Further Testing for significance

TESTING

H0: μ = 729.157 H1: μ < 729.157

Bootstrapping:

99% significance z=

x̄ =704.602

sd = 645.998

As we have found that this causes a significant chnage to the mean we will continue by discarding all data points of non-functioning days to remove this confounding variable from other variable investigations.

HOLIDAYS

bike_data%>%
  group_by(Holiday)%>%
  summarise( 
          min_rent = min(Rented.Bike.Count),
          avg_rent = mean(Rented.Bike.Count, na.rm= TRUE),
          med_rent = median(Rented.Bike.Count),
          max_rent = max(Rented.Bike.Count),
          sd_rent = sd(Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.25, Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.5, Rented.Bike.Count),
          quantile(probs = 0.75, Rented.Bike.Count))
## # A tibble: 2 × 9
##   Holiday    min_rent avg_rent med_rent max_rent sd_rent quantile(probs = 0.25…¹
##   <chr>         <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <int>   <dbl>                   <dbl>
## 1 Holiday           0     500.     240      2400    571.                    106.
## 2 No Holiday        0     715.     524.     3556    647.                    200 
## # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​`quantile(probs = 0.25, Rented.Bike.Count)`
## # ℹ 2 more variables: `quantile(probs = 0.5, Rented.Bike.Count)` <dbl>,
## #   `quantile(probs = 0.75, Rented.Bike.Count)` <dbl>

From the data we can see on average that the number of bike rentals decrease during holidays from a mean of 715.2280 to 499.7569, this is significant as it suggests that the majority of rentals perhaps are related to comuttors travel to and from work/ school, further suggesting that rentals mainly occur among the working-aged demographic.

This significant higher rental rates on no holidays are significant on all of the statistics.

This perhaps suggest the Seoul government should campaign to increase bike rentals on holiday days more.

bike_data %>%
  drop_na(Rented.Bike.Count,Holiday) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Holiday, y = Rented.Bike.Count)) +
  geom_boxplot(color = "blue",
               fill = "skyblue") +
  labs(x = "Holiday",
       y = "Rented Bike Count",
       title = "Relaionship between Rental and Holidays") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

However from the graph, it also becomes apparent that there are many more outliers on non-holiday says. This could suggest bike rentals vary perhaps more greatly on these days as suggested by the greater standard deviation of 646.8791 to 570.7728.

Peraps in future it may be prudent to explore the clientel of bike renters in Seoul or even the concentration of rentals around Soeul to ensure bikes are available in the most relavant locations.

Seasons: XXX We can see that the graph of rental and seasons shows a right-skewed distribuion. Winter has the lowest number of rental and summer has the highest (too cold for people to go out?) Number of rental are widely spread out in autumn, spring, summer and highly concentrated in winter. (people have same mindset in winter)

Exploring Meteorological Variables

TEMPERATURE

bike_data %>%
  drop_na(Rented.Bike.Count, Temperature.蚓.) %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = Temperature.蚓., y = Rented.Bike.Count)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1, color = "pink") +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE, colour = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Temperature",
       y = "Rented Bike Count",
       title = "Relationship between Rental and Temperature") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Bike_data_temp_lm <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(Rented.Bike.Count ~ Temperature.蚓.,
    data = bike_data)

tidy(Bike_data_temp_lm)
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##   term            estimate std.error statistic   p.value
##   <chr>              <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
## 1 (Intercept)        330.      8.54       38.6 1.29e-301
## 2 Temperature.蚓.     29.1     0.486      59.8 0
glance(Bike_data_temp_lm)
## # A tibble: 1 × 12
##   r.squared adj.r.squared sigma statistic p.value    df  logLik     AIC     BIC
##       <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1     0.290         0.290  543.     3578.       0     1 -67600. 135205. 135226.
## # ℹ 3 more variables: deviance <dbl>, df.residual <int>, nobs <int>

Regressionline Temperature: Rental is higher between 20-40 Concentrated in low temperature and Spread away in high temperature(It’s not necessary to rent bike in a low temperature, and it depends on other factors in high temperature) Positive correlation

Exploring Temporal Variables Part 2

DAYS

bike_data %>%
  drop_na(Rented.Bike.Count, Date) %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Bikes_Day = mean(Rented.Bike.Count),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Date, y = Mean_Bikes_Day)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    x = "Date",
    y = "Mean Bikes Rented",
    title = "Mean Bike Rentals by Day")

Interpretation

WEEKDAYS

bike_data %>%

  mutate(Day = weekdays(as.Date(Date))) %>%
  group_by(Day, Seasons) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Bikes_Day = mean(Rented.Bike.Count),

  ggplot(aes(x = Day, y = Mean_Bikes_Day, fill = Seasons)) +

Further Explorations

RAINFALL + TEMP + RENT Predicting the LINEAR REGGRESSION

bike_data_rain <- bike_data %>%
  select(
    Temperature.蚓.,
    Rainfall.mm.,
    Snowfall..cm.,
    Rented.Bike.Count) %>%
  drop_na()

bike_data_rain <- bike_data_rain %>%
  mutate(
    Precipitation = case_when(
      Rainfall.mm. > 0 | Snowfall..cm. > 0 ~ "Precipitation",
      TRUE ~ "No Precipitation"),
    Precipitation = factor(
      Precipitation,
      levels = c("No Precipitation", "Precipitation")))

Bike_data_rain_lm <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  fit(Rented.Bike.Count ~ Temperature.蚓.,
    data = bike_data_rain)

tidy(Bike_data_rain_lm)
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##   term            estimate std.error statistic   p.value

library(knitr)

Bike_data_rain <- bike_data %>%
  select(
    Temperature.蚓.,
    Rainfall.mm.,
    Snowfall..cm.,
    Rented.Bike.Count) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    Precipitation = case_when(
      Rainfall.mm. > 0 | Snowfall..cm. > 0 ~ "Precipitation",
      TRUE ~ "No Precipitation"),
    Precipitation = factor(
      Precipitation,
      levels = c("No Precipitation", "Precipitation")))

set.seed(1234)

Bike_data_rain_split <- initial_split(Bike_data_rain)

Bike_data_rain_train <- training(Bike_data_rain_split)
Bike_data_rain_test  <- testing(Bike_data_rain_split)

Bike_data_rain_rec_1 <- recipe(
  Precipitation ~ Temperature.蚓.,
  data = Bike_data_rain_train
)

Bike_data_rain_mod_1 <- logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine("glm")

Bike_data_rain_wflow_1 <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(Bike_data_rain_mod_1) %>%
  add_recipe(Bike_data_rain_rec_1)

Bike_data_rain_fit_1 <- Bike_data_rain_wflow_1 %>%
  fit(data = Bike_data_rain_train)

tidy(Bike_data_rain_fit_1)
## # A tibble: 2 × 5
##   term            estimate std.error statistic   p.value
##   <chr>              <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
## 1 (Intercept)      -1.62     0.0484      -33.4 1.08e-244
## 2 Temperature.蚓.  -0.0481   0.00345     -13.9 3.88e- 44
bike_data_rain_pred_1 <- predict(
  Bike_data_rain_fit_1,
  Bike_data_rain_test,
  type = "prob"
)

bike_data_rain_pred_1 <- bind_cols(
  Bike_data_rain_test %>% select(Precipitation),
  bike_data_rain_pred_1
)

bike_data_rain_pred_1 <- bind_cols(
  Bike_data_rain_test %>% select(Rainfall.mm.),
  bike_data_rain_pred_1
)


bike_data_rain_roc_1 <- bike_data_rain_pred_1 %>%
  roc_curve(
    truth = Precipitation,
    .pred_Precipitation,
    event_level = "second"
  )

autoplot(bike_data_rain_roc_1) +
  labs(
    title = "ROC Curve - Logistic Regression Model 1",
    x = "1 - Specificity (False Positive Rate)",
    y = "Sensitivity (True Positive Rate)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

MODE DATA OF TIMES OF DAY 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVAL THROUGH BOOTSRAPPING - MODE HOURS IN THE MORNING AND AFTERNOON FOR BIKE RENTAL

library(infer)
daily_modes <- bike_data %>%
  mutate(
    Time_Period = if_else(Hour < 12, "AM", "PM")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Date, Time_Period) %>%
  slice_max(
    order_by = Rented.Bike.Count,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Date, Time_Period, Mode_Hour = Hour)

daily_modes
## # A tibble: 730 × 3
##    Date       Time_Period Mode_Hour
##    <date>     <chr>           <int>
##  1 2017-12-01 AM                  8
##  2 2017-12-01 PM                 18
##  3 2017-12-02 AM                 11
##  4 2017-12-02 PM                 16
##  5 2017-12-03 AM                  0
##  6 2017-12-03 PM                 15
##  7 2017-12-04 AM                  8
##  8 2017-12-04 PM                 18
##  9 2017-12-05 AM                  8
## 10 2017-12-05 PM                 18
## # ℹ 720 more rows
set.seed(1234)

bootstrap_means <- daily_modes %>%
  group_by(Time_Period) %>%
  summarise(
    Sample_Means = list(
      replicate(
        1500,
        mean(
          sample(
            Mode_Hour,
            size = n(),
            replace = TRUE
          )
        )
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bootstrap_summary <- bootstrap_means %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Mean_of_Sample_Means = mean(Sample_Means),
    SD_of_Sample_Means = sd(Sample_Means)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

bootstrap_summary
## # A tibble: 2 × 4
##   Time_Period Sample_Means  Mean_of_Sample_Means SD_of_Sample_Means
##   <chr>       <list>                       <dbl>              <dbl>
## 1 AM          <dbl [1,500]>                 6.95             0.198 
## 2 PM          <dbl [1,500]>                17.4              0.0989
bootstrap_summary <- bootstrap_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Lower_CI = Mean_of_Sample_Means -
      1.96 * SD_of_Sample_Means,

    Upper_CI = Mean_of_Sample_Means +
      1.96 * SD_of_Sample_Means
  )

bootstrap_summary
## # A tibble: 2 × 6
##   Time_Period Sample_Means  Mean_of_Sample_Means SD_of_Sample_Means Lower_CI
##   <chr>       <list>                       <dbl>              <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1 AM          <dbl [1,500]>                 6.95             0.198      6.56
## 2 PM          <dbl [1,500]>                17.4              0.0989    17.2 
## # ℹ 1 more variable: Upper_CI <dbl>
bootstrap_means %>%
  unnest(Sample_Means) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Sample_Means)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 30
  ) +
  geom_density(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~Time_Period, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Distribution of Mean Peak Rental Hours",
    x = "Mean Peak Rental Hour",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

max_hours <- bike_data %>%
  group_by(Date) %>%
  filter( 6<=Hour & Hour<=11) %>%
  filter(Rented.Bike.Count == max(Rented.Bike.Count))

library(infer)
boot_hours <- max_hours %>%
  specify(response=Hour) %>%
  generate(reps=5000, type ="bootstrap") %>%
  calculate(stat="mean")

ggplot(data = boot_hours, mapping = aes(x = stat)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.025) +
  labs(title = "Bootstrap distribution of means")

boot_hours %>%
  summarize(lower = quantile(stat, 0.025),
            upper = quantile(stat, 0.975))
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   lower upper
##   <dbl> <dbl>
## 1  8.73  9.01
#we are 95% confident that the mean time to travel to work is between 8.73 hours and 9.02 hours
